quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on missiles: L3Harris is 'talking about $20 billion of new contracts'; the first undefinitized contract action came the day before ('It went out $4.7 billion'), and of the PAC-3 award he said '$4.6 billion. We didn't put any of the escalators or anything in that. That's 80% of the PAC-3 demand', and '100% of all the DACS as well' (both dollar figures as spoken). L3Harris has '$2.2 billion out in either supply chain or building commitments' made ahead of contract with the Department of War, ultimately about 100 different buildings in Camden and elsewhere; at Orange, construction crews were at one point pulled to a data-center job before the Department of War restored L3Harris's priority. It is generally sole sourced on most if not all of the major missile programs it supplies components to, has a seeker that 'can go on PAC-3 today', and the electronics content L3Harris put in is 30% of the missiles business today, probably 35%-40% after the divestiture.
quarterly_data.figure: about $20 billion of new contracts in negotiation; PAC-3 award $4.6 billion (80% of PAC-3 demand, 100% of DACS); $2.2 billion of supply-chain / building commitments; about 100 buildings

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on supply: in Communications & Spectrum Dominance 'the people that are buying all the stuff for AI are now impacting your radio capability as far as manufacturing it' - materials for electronic boards have become harder to get ('the AI demand is huge'), tied to 'really two vendors' and 'fourth tier materials'; L3Harris has gone dual source on different vendors and engaged the Department of War with non-U.S. suppliers, and the vendors have said they are prioritizing L3Harris. The CSD second-half revenue ramp still holds but is 'probably more fourth quarter weighted', with the third quarter flatter.

CFO Ken Sharp on Space & Mission Systems: organic growth was 15% in the first half and the segment will probably do better this year than expected; it is split roughly a third space, a third ISR aircraft and a third cyber and other. L3Harris has been the prime on all five missile-tracking / missile-warning awards (AMDT-3 is the fifth) and has about 72 satellites left to get into space; space margins are below the segment average, with conservative booking rates and more management reserve, and last quarter's $55 million charge was on a program signed a relatively long time ago. ISR margins are closer to the segment average, with a couple of very large new aircraft-type wins being worked through, including new international variants.
quarterly_data.figure: SMS first-half organic growth 15%; about 72 satellites left to launch; $55 million charge last quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Sharp on radios and electronic warfare: Falcon IV will move to Falcon V, 'a whole new radio' about half the size with better battery life and more capacity, rolling out around the end of next year (international customers move from Falcon III to Falcon IV); U.S. radio modernization is at '40-plus percent'. Counter-UAS has a '$1 billion in pipeline' - the VAMPIRE system fires '$30,000 missiles at drones' with a kill rate of 'about 80%' and has been fielded in Ukraine - and L3Harris is working with SOCOM on Wraith Shield-type software jamming. Next Generation Jammer is on schedule and on price, in a cost-type development phase with lower margins. Margin focus: a clean 16% margin without asset-sale gains, fewer EAC charges through management reserve, missile volumes going '3x, 4x, 5x, 10x' on different programs, and the former Remington facility in Huntsville to dual-source parts where suppliers create issues.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. modernization 40-plus percent; counter-UAS pipeline $1 billion; VAMPIRE kill rate about 80%; 16% margin target
